skill.name: child-agent-ops
skill.description: Standardizes child agent launch, task assignment, reporting, and safe operation for Codex-based development workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate child agents with clear roles, logs, checkpoints, review handoffs, and completion reports.
skill.author: A-Genno

content.value_statement: Multi-agent work can become unclear without task scope, logs, and review gates. This skill provides a structured workflow for delegating, tracking, and reporting child-agent tasks.
actual_capabilities: Defines leader, implementation, and review agent responsibilities.
Provides launch criteria for independent implementation, research, and validation tasks.
Supplies a standard workflow for assigning scope, checkpoints, reports, and handoffs.
Includes checklists for start, execution, completion, and high-risk confirmation points.
Provides Markdown templates for task reports and child agent launch logs.
Requires review agent activation after code changes.
limitations: It is an operating guide, not an agent orchestration runtime.
It does not create agents or enforce permissions by itself.
It assumes users already have access to Codex or compatible agent tools.
It does not replace project-specific security or release approval rules.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Implementation
use_cases.description: Split independent coding work into scoped child-agent tasks with owners, completion criteria, and checkpoint reports.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Handoffs
use_cases.description: Trigger a review agent after code changes and capture findings, blockers, and next actions in a consistent report.

use_cases.title: Run Research And Validation Tasks
use_cases.description: Assign investigation, performance, or security validation work to a focused agent with clear reporting expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Child Agent Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use child-agent-ops to define the goal, completion condition, owner role, expected duration, and report format for this task: [task].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use child-agent-ops to split this project into independent implementation, research, and validation tasks. Include dependencies and checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Review Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use child-agent-ops to prepare a review-agent handoff for these changes. Include scope, risks, expected findings, and completion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Recover A Blocked Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use child-agent-ops to assess this blocked multi-agent workflow. Identify owners, unresolved risks, next actions, and required leader decisions.

output_examples.input: Plan child agents for a small API cleanup.
output: Leader defines the cleanup goal, completion condition, and priority.
Implementation agent handles scoped code changes and reports blockers immediately.
Review agent checks changed files and reports findings before completion.

output_examples.input: Report status for an implementation child agent.
output: Purpose: complete the assigned implementation scope.
Current state: core changes are complete, validation remains open.
Problem: one compatibility risk needs leader confirmation.
Next action: request confirmation, then run review.

best_practices: Define the goal, completion condition, owner role, and expected duration before launch.
Share blockers, security risks, billing changes, and data deletion risks before proceeding.
Start a review agent whenever code is changed or created.
anti_patterns: Do not launch child agents for tasks that cannot be separated safely.
Do not let implementation agents expand scope without leader visibility.
Do not close work without reporting outputs, risks, and next actions.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate child agents for implementation, research, validation, and review work.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance, checklists, and report templates for users to follow.

faq.question: When should I use a child agent?
faq.answer: Use one when a task is independent, specialized, and faster to complete in parallel.

faq.question: When should I avoid a child agent?
faq.answer: Avoid one when the work is tightly coupled or coordination cost exceeds the benefit.

faq.question: How does it handle risky changes?
faq.answer: It requires leader confirmation for unclear specifications, compatibility risks, security changes, billing changes, and data deletion.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes general agent coordination patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
